data.long_meaning: Achilles (Ἀχιλλεύς) is a name of Greek origin meaning “Grief of the people (proposed); the etymology is debated”. Commonly analysed as a compound of ἄχος (akhos) 'grief, pain' and λαός (laos) 'people, host of fighting men' - 'grief of the people'. The derivation is debated and a pre-Greek origin has been proposed. Its root is Greek Ἀχιλλεύς (Akhilleus), commonly analysed as ἄχος (akhos) 'grief, pain' + λαός (laos) 'people, host'. Achilles is a Greek mythological name, not a Biblical or Christian name.

faq.a: No. The name does not occur in the Bible. It is a Greek mythological name.

faq.a: The meaning “Grief of the people (proposed); the etymology is debated” is supported by Greek mythology: the hero of the Iliad. Not a Biblical or Christian name in origin. Confidence: HIGH.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Achilles?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Achilles total 69, reducing to 6. Number 6 is traditionally associated with responsibility, care and harmony. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Achilles?
faq.a: Variants and alternative forms include Akhilleus, Achille, Aquiles.

faq.q: What is the transliteration of Achilles?
faq.a: Achilles is transliterated as Akhilleús.

faq.q: How many syllables does Achilles have?
faq.a: Achilles has 3 syllables.

faq.q: What are the spiritual connotations of Achilles?
faq.a: Any spiritual significance attached to Achilles is interpretive. Its documented core is the lexical meaning “Grief of the people (proposed); the etymology is debated”, and readings built on that meaning are presented as tradition rather than as religious doctrine.

faq.q: Where is the name Achilles used today?
faq.a: Achilles circulates chiefly in Ancient Greek, English, Latin naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
